#### Responsive Align Items

The align-items property supports responsive breakpoints, allowing you to change vertical alignment at different screen sizes using `align-items-xs`, `align-items-sm`, `align-items-md`, `align-items-lg`, and `align-items-xl`.

    react: `// Start on mobile, center on tablets and up
<PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" alignItems="start" alignItemsMd="center" minHeight="100px">
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>

// Center on mobile, stretch on desktop
<PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" alignItems="center" alignItemsLg="stretch" minHeight="100px">
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item A</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item B</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<!-- Start on mobile, center on tablets and up -->
<pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="start" align-items-md="center" min-height="100px">
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</pds-box>
</pds-box>

<!-- Center on mobile, stretch on desktop -->
<pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="center" align-items-lg="stretch" min-height="100px">
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item A</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item B</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box direction="column" gap="sm">
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="start" align-items-md="center" min-height="100px">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="center" align-items-lg="stretch" min-height="100px">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item A</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item B</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
  </pds-box>

#### Common Align Items Patterns

```html
<!-- Center content on mobile, align to top on desktop -->
<pds-box align-items="center" align-items-lg="start">
  <pds-text>Content</pds-text>
</pds-box>

<!-- Stretch items on mobile for touch targets, center on desktop -->
<pds-box align-items="stretch" align-items-md="center">
  <pds-button>Action 1</pds-button>
  <pds-button>Action 2</pds-button>
</pds-box>
```

### Align Self

Defines how an individual box aligns itself within its parent container, overriding the parent's `align-items` setting.

Layout impact:
- `start`: Box aligns to the start (top for column, left for row)
- `center`: Box aligns to the center
- `end`: Box aligns to the end (bottom for column, right for row)
- `baseline`: Box aligns to its text baseline
- `stretch`: Box stretches to fill the container (default)

#### Basic Align Self Examples

    react: `<PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" alignItems="center" minHeight="150px" gap="sm">
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" alignSelf="start">Start</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" alignSelf="center">Center</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" alignSelf="end">End</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" alignSelf="stretch">Stretch</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" alignSelf="baseline">Baseline</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="center" min-height="150px" gap="sm">
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="start">Start</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="center">Center</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="end">End</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="stretch">Stretch</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="baseline">Baseline</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="center" min-height="150px" gap="sm">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="start">Start</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="center">Center</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="end">End</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="stretch">Stretch</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="baseline">Baseline</pds-box>
  </pds-box>

#### Responsive Align Self

The align-self property supports responsive breakpoints, allowing you to change individual box alignment at different screen sizes using `align-self-xs`, `align-self-sm`, `align-self-md`, `align-self-lg`, and `align-self-xl`.

    react: `<PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" alignItems="center" minHeight="120px" gap="sm">
  {/* This box changes from start on mobile to center on tablets+ */}
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" alignSelf="start" alignSelfMd="center">
    Responsive Box 1
  </PdsBox>

  {/* This box changes from stretch on mobile to end on desktop */}
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" alignSelf="stretch" alignSelfLg="end">
    Responsive Box 2
  </PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="center" min-height="120px" gap="sm">
  <!-- This box changes from start on mobile to center on tablets+ -->
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="start" align-self-md="center">
    Responsive Box 1
  </pds-box>

  <!-- This box changes from stretch on mobile to end on desktop -->
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="stretch" align-self-lg="end">
    Responsive Box 2
  </pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" align-items="center" min-height="120px" gap="sm">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="start" align-self-md="center">
      Responsive Box 1
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs" align-self="stretch" align-self-lg="end">
      Responsive Box 2
    </pds-box>
  </pds-box>

#### Common Align Self Patterns

```html
<!-- Individual item that stands out on mobile, blends in on desktop -->
<pds-box align-self="center" align-self-lg="start">
  <pds-button variant="primary">Call to Action</pds-button>
</pds-box>

<!-- Sidebar that stretches on mobile, aligns to top on desktop -->
<pds-box align-self="stretch" align-self-md="start">
  <pds-text>Sidebar Content</pds-text>
</pds-box>
```

### Justify Content

Defines the horizontal alignment of the box items.

Layout impact:
- `start`: Items pack toward the start (left for row, top for column)
- `center`: Items pack toward the center
- `end`: Items pack toward the end (right for row, bottom for column)
- `space-between`: Items are evenly distributed with first at start, last at end
- `space-around`: Items are evenly distributed with equal space around them
- `space-evenly`: Items are evenly distributed with equal space around them

#### Basic Justify Content Examples

    react: `<PdsBox direction="column" gap="sm">
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="start">
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  </PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="center">
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  </PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="end">
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  </PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="space-between">
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  </PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="space-around">
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  </PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="space-evenly">
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  </PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box direction="column" gap="sm">
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="start">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  </pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="center">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  </pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="end">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  </pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="space-between">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  </pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="space-around">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  </pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="space-evenly">
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  </pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box direction="column" gap="sm">
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="start">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="center">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="end">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="space-between">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="space-around">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="space-evenly">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
  </pds-box>

#### Responsive Justify Content

The justify-content property supports responsive breakpoints, allowing you to change alignment at different screen sizes using `justify-content-xs`, `justify-content-sm`, `justify-content-md`, `justify-content-lg`, and `justify-content-xl`.

    react: `// Center on mobile, space-between on tablets and up
<PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="center" justifyContentMd="space-between">
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>

// Start on mobile, center on desktop
<PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" justifyContent="start" justifyContentLg="center">
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item A</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item B</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<!-- Center on mobile, space-between on tablets and up -->
<pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="center" justify-content-md="space-between">
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</pds-box>
</pds-box>

<!-- Start on mobile, center on desktop -->
<pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="start" justify-content-lg="center">
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item A</pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item B</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box direction="column" gap="sm">
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="center" justify-content-md="space-between">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" justify-content="start" justify-content-lg="center">
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item A</pds-box>
      <pds-box flex="none" border="true" padding="xs">Item B</pds-box>
    </pds-box>
  </pds-box>

#### Common Justify Content Patterns

```html
<!-- Center buttons on mobile, space them apart on desktop -->
<pds-box justify-content="center" justify-content-lg="space-between">
  <pds-button>Cancel</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="primary">Save</pds-button>
</pds-box>

<!-- Stack navigation items on mobile, spread them on tablet+ -->
<pds-box justify-content="start" justify-content-sm="space-around">
  <pds-link>Home</pds-link>
  <pds-link>About</pds-link>
  <pds-link>Contact</pds-link>
</pds-box>
```

### Size

Grid system:
- Uses a 12-column grid system
- Values range from 1-12 (e.g., `6` = 50% width, `12` = 100% width)
- Most effective when used inside `pds-row` containers
- Responsive variants available: `size-xs`, `size-sm`, `size-md`, `size-lg`, `size-xl`

### Flex
The `flex` prop controls how a box grows or shrinks within its container. It accepts both predefined values and custom CSS flex values.

> **⚠️ CRITICAL CONSTRAINT:** The `flex` prop **ONLY** works when the parent element is another `pds-box` component. It does **NOT** work when the parent is `pds-row` or other elements, as those components use different layout systems. Always ensure the immediate parent is a `pds-box` when using flex properties.

#### Predefined Values
- `none` - The box will not grow or shrink (equivalent to `flex: 0 0 auto`)
- `grow` - The box will grow to fill available space (equivalent to `flex: 1 1 0`)
- `shrink` - The box will shrink when space is limited (equivalent to `flex: 0 1 auto`)

    react: `<PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" flex="none">Flex: none</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" flex="grow">Flex: grow</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" flex="shrink">Flex: shrink</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" flex="none">Flex: none</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" flex="grow">Flex: grow</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" flex="shrink">Flex: shrink</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" flex="none">Flex: none</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" flex="grow">Flex: grow</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" flex="shrink">Flex: shrink</pds-box>
  </pds-box>

#### Custom Flex Values
You can also provide custom CSS flex values as strings for precise control:

    react: `<PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" flex="1">Flex: 1</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" flex="2">Flex: 2</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" flex="0 1 100px">Flex: 0 1 100px</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" flex="1">Flex: 1</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" flex="2">Flex: 2</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" flex="0 1 100px">Flex: 0 1 100px</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" flex="1">Flex: 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" flex="2">Flex: 2</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" flex="0 1 100px">Flex: 0 1 100px</pds-box>
  </pds-box>

Common custom flex patterns:
- `"1"`: Equal flex growth (equivalent to `flex: 1 1 0`)
- `"2"`: Grows twice as much as `flex="1"` items
- `"0 1 auto"`: No growth, can shrink, size based on content
- `"0 0 200px"`: Fixed 200px width, no grow/shrink

> **⚠️ REMINDER:** These flex properties only work when the immediate parent is a `pds-box` component, **NOT** when inside `pds-row` or other containers.

#### ❌ Incorrect Usage (Will NOT Work)
```tsx
// DON'T DO THIS - flex props are ignored inside pds-row
<pds-row>
  <pds-box flex="grow">This flex prop will be ignored</pds-box>
</pds-row>
```

#### ✅ Correct Usage (Will Work)
```tsx
// DO THIS - flex props work inside another pds-box
<pds-box>
  <pds-box flex="grow">This flex prop will work</pds-box>
</pds-box>
```

### Wrap
Control whether flex items wrap to new lines when they don't fit in the container:

#### Wrap Options
- `false` (default): Items stay on one line and may overflow (equivalent to `flex-wrap: nowrap`)
- `true`: Items wrap to new lines as needed (equivalent to `flex-wrap: wrap`)

#### No Wrap (default)
    react: `
  <PdsBox wrap={false} gap="sm" min-width="250px">
    <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 1</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 2</PdsBox>
    <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 3</PdsBox>
  </PdsBox>
`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box wrap="false" gap="sm" min-width="250px">
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 2</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 3</pds-box>
  </pds-box>`
  <pds-box wrap="false" gap="sm" min-width="250px">
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 2</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Long Item 3</pds-box>
  </pds-box>

#### Wrap

    react: `<PdsBox wrap={true} gap="sm" min-width="300px">
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Item 1</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Item 2</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Item 3</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Item 4</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm">Item 5</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box wrap="true" gap="sm" min-width="300px">
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 1</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 2</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 3</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 4</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 5</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box wrap="true" gap="sm" min-width="300px" >
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 2</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 3</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 4</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm">Item 5</pds-box>
  </pds-box>

## Responsive Properties

All the following properties support responsive variants that allow different values at different screen sizes. This enables fine-grained control over layout behavior across devices.

### Responsive Breakpoints

For detailed information about responsive breakpoints and how they work with the layout system, see the [Layout documentation](/docs/components-layout--docs#responsive-breakpoints).

### Responsive Gap

Control spacing between items at different breakpoints:

    react: `<PdsBox gap="xs" gap-md="lg" border="true" padding="sm">
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box gap="xs" gap-md="lg" border="true" padding="sm">
  <pds-box border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box gap="xs" gap-md="lg" border="true" padding="sm">
    <pds-box border="true" padding="xs">Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="xs">Item 2</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="xs">Item 3</pds-box>
  </pds-box>

### Responsive Padding

Control internal spacing at different breakpoints:

    react: `<PdsBox padding="xs" padding-md="lg" border="true">
  Responsive padding content
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box padding="xs" padding-md="lg" border="true">
  Responsive padding content
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box padding="xs" padding-md="lg" border="true">
    Responsive padding content
  </pds-box>

### Responsive Wrap

Control flex wrap behavior at different breakpoints:

    react: `<PdsBox wrap="false" wrap-md="true" gap="sm" min-width="400px" border="true" padding="sm">
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 1</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 2</PdsBox>
  <PdsBox border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 3</PdsBox>
</PdsBox>`,
    webComponent: `<pds-box wrap="false" wrap-md="true" gap="sm" min-width="400px" border="true" padding="sm">
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 1</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 2</pds-box>
  <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 3</pds-box>
</pds-box>`
  <pds-box wrap="false" wrap-md="true" gap="sm" min-width="400px" border="true" padding="sm">
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 1</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 2</pds-box>
    <pds-box border="true" padding="sm" min-width="150px">Long Item 3</pds-box>
  </pds-box>

### Available Responsive Properties

All of these properties support responsive variants with `-xs`, `-sm`, `-md`, `-lg`, `-xl` suffixes:

- **gap**: `gap`, `gap-xs`, `gap-sm`, `gap-md`, `gap-lg`, `gap-xl`
- **padding**: `padding`, `padding-xs`, `padding-sm`, `padding-md`, `padding-lg`, `padding-xl`
- **padding-block-start**: `padding-block-start`, `padding-block-start-xs`, `padding-block-start-sm`, etc.
- **padding-block-end**: `padding-block-end`, `padding-block-end-xs`, `padding-block-end-sm`, etc.
- **padding-inline-start**: `padding-inline-start`, `padding-inline-start-xs`, `padding-inline-start-sm`, etc.
- **padding-inline-end**: `padding-inline-end`, `padding-inline-end-xs`, `padding-inline-end-sm`, etc.
- **margin-block-start**: `margin-block-start`, `margin-block-start-xs`, `margin-block-start-sm`, etc.
- **margin-block-end**: `margin-block-end`, `margin-block-end-xs`, `margin-block-end-sm`, etc.
- **margin-inline-start**: `margin-inline-start`, `margin-inline-start-xs`, `margin-inline-start-sm`, etc.
- **margin-inline-end**: `margin-inline-end`, `margin-inline-end-xs`, `margin-inline-end-sm`, etc.
- **wrap**: `wrap`, `wrap-xs`, `wrap-sm`, `wrap-md`, `wrap-lg`, `wrap-xl`
- **auto**: `auto`, `auto-xs`, `auto-sm`, `auto-md`, `auto-lg`, `auto-xl`
- **fit**: `fit`, `fit-xs`, `fit-sm`, `fit-md`, `fit-lg`, `fit-xl`

### Layout Properties
`pds-box` not only allows for custom element properties, but it also allows for a flexible layout system. The layout system is based on the [CSS Flexbox specification](https://drafts.csswg.org/css-flexbox/) and can be view on the [Layouts](/docs/components-layout--docs) page

## Direction Troubleshooting

### Problem: Items Not Arranging as Expected

#### Issue: Content stacking when you want side-by-side
```tsx
// ❌ Problem: Buttons stack vertically instead of horizontally
<PdsBox direction="column">
  <PdsButton>Save</PdsButton>
  <PdsButton>Cancel</PdsButton>
</PdsBox>
```

**Solution:** Remove `direction="column"` or use `direction="row"` (default):
```tsx
// ✅ Solution: Buttons appear side by side
<PdsBox>
  <PdsButton>Save</PdsButton>
  <PdsButton>Cancel</PdsButton>
</PdsBox>
```

#### Issue: Content appearing side-by-side when you want stacking
```tsx
// ❌ Problem: Title and text appear next to each other
<PdsBox>
  <h1>Page Title</h1>
  <p>Description text</p>
</PdsBox>
```

**Solution:** Add `direction="column"`:
```tsx
// ✅ Solution: Title appears above description
<PdsBox direction="column">
  <h1>Page Title</h1>
  <p>Description text</p>
</PdsBox>
```

### Quick Decision Tree for LLMs:

> ** Direction Decision Rules:**
> 1. **Are you building a page/card/form?** → Use `direction="column"`
> 2. **Are you placing buttons/badges/icons together?** → Use default (no direction needed)
> 3. **Are children meant to stack vertically?** → Use `direction="column"`
> 4. **Are children meant to flow horizontally?** → Use default (no direction needed)

## Responsive Sizing Strategies & Examples

The `pds-box` component uses a mobile-first approach to responsive sizing. This means that styles cascade up from smaller breakpoints to larger ones, unless overridden at a specific breakpoint.

### Understanding the Cascade

- The base `size` prop sets the default width that applies to all breakpoints unless overridden
- Breakpoint-specific props (`size-xs`, `size-sm`, etc.) override the base size at their respective breakpoints and larger
- Each breakpoint-specific prop overrides any sizes set by smaller breakpoint props

### Breakpoint Behavior

See the [Responsive Breakpoints](#responsive-breakpoints) section above for detailed breakpoint ranges.

### Common Patterns

#### Stacking on small screens, columns on larger screens

```html
<!-- Full width on mobile, half width on tablets and up -->
<pds-box size="12" size-md="6"></pds-box>

<!-- Full width on mobile, one-third width on tablets and up -->
<pds-box size="12" size-md="4"></pds-box>
```

#### Explicit full-width layout on small screens

```html
<!-- Explicit full width on mobile, different widths at different breakpoints -->
<pds-box size="12" size-sm="6" size-lg="4"></pds-box>
```

#### When to use/avoid the base `size` prop

If you want consistent sizing across all breakpoints:

```html
<!-- Same width across all breakpoints -->
<pds-box size="6"></pds-box>
```

If you need different sizes at different breakpoints:

```html
<!-- Different widths at different breakpoints -->
<pds-box size-sm="12" size-md="6" size-lg="4"></pds-box>
```

### Default Behavior

When no size props are provided, the box will use `flex-grow: 1` and `flex-basis: 0`, allowing it to grow and fill available space while maintaining equal widths with other flex items.

```html
<!-- These boxes will share available space equally -->
<pds-row>
  <pds-box></pds-box>
  <pds-box></pds-box>
</pds-row>
```

# Button

Source: https://github.com/kajabi/pine/blob/main/libs/core/src/components/pds-button/docs/pds-button.mdx

import * as stories from '../stories/pds-button.stories.js';

import {DocArgsTable, DocCanvas} from '@pine-ds/doc-components';

<StatusBadge component="pds-button" />

# Button

A button is an interactive element that can be clicked to perform various actions such as triggering an event, submitting data, or navigating to a different location.

## Guidelines

### When to use

- Communicating an action that will occur (e.g. saving a page).
- Triggering or enabling an action, such as submitting requested information (e.g. forms).
- Progressing or regressing a user through a step in a flow (e.g. modals).

### When not to use
- When space is limited consider an IconButton.

### Accessibility

While accessible out of the box, there are some best practices to keep in mind when using the component:

- Use helpful text to describe the button's action even if this text is expected to be visually hidden (e.g. "submit form" or "delete account"). Visually hidden text will still be read by screen readers.
- Buttons should not disable tabbing or keyboard navigation.
- Disabled buttons will not be read by screen readers.

### Buttons vs Links

In many current web design patterns, buttons and links have evolved to look visually identical. However, for best practices, the fundamental differences between the two should be considered before using. Links are used to navigate the user to another page. Buttons are used to perform an action on the current page or submit a form.

### Icon Slots

The `start` and `end` slots allow icons to be placed before and after the button text but will be hidden when `loading` is true. For more information on web component slots, see the [MDN documentation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_components/Using_templates_and_slots#adding_flexibility_with_slots).

```html
<pds-button>
  <pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="trash"></pds-icon>
  Start Icon
</pds-button>
```

```html
<pds-button>
  End Icon
  <pds-icon slot="end" aria-hidden="true" name="trash"></pds-icon>
</pds-button>
```

## Properties

<DocArgsTable componentName="pds-button" docSource={components}/>

## Examples

### Primary

The default button, intended to be used with affirmative actions such as submitting, continuing, and saving.

    react: `
    <PdsButton>Primary</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton disabled="true">Disabled</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="trash"></PdsIcon>Icon</PdsButton>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-button>Primary</pds-button>
    <pds-button disabled="true">Disabled</pds-button>
    <pds-button><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="trash"></pds-icon>Icon</pds-button>
    `
  <pds-button>Primary</pds-button>
  <pds-button disabled="true">Disabled</pds-button>
  <pds-button><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="trash"></pds-icon>Icon</pds-button>

### Secondary

Secondary button variant, intended to be used as back buttons, for saving drafts, or cancelling actions.

  <pds-button variant="secondary">Secondary</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="secondary" disabled="true">Disabled</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="secondary"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="trash"></pds-icon>Icon</pds-button>

### Tertiary

Tertiary button variant, intended to be used for low-emphasis actions or when a subtler button style is needed.

    `
  <pds-button variant="tertiary">Tertiary</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="tertiary" disabled="true">Disabled</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="tertiary"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="trash"></pds-icon>Icon</pds-button>

### Accent

Accent button variant, intended to be used for special emphasis or when higher contrast is needed.

    react: `

Full width buttons are intended to be used when the button needs to take up the full width of its container.

    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-button variant="primary" full-width="true">Full Width</pds-button>
    `

### Loading

The loading prop allows a `pds-button` to display a loading state.

    react: `
    <PdsButton variant="primary" loading="true">Loading</PdsButton>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-button variant="primary" loading="true">Loading</pds-button>
    `
  <pds-button variant="primary" loading="true">Loading</pds-button>

#### Customizing Loader Color

The loader color can be customized using CSS parts.

    react: `
    <style>{\`
      .custom-loader-accent::part(loader-svg) {
        color: var(--pine-color-accent);
      }
      .custom-loader-danger::part(loader-svg) {
        color: var(--pine-color-danger);
      }
    \`}</style>

    <PdsButton className="custom-loader-accent" variant="primary" loading="true">Accent Loader</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton className="custom-loader-danger" variant="secondary" loading="true">Danger Loader</PdsButton>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <style>
      .custom-loader-accent::part(loader-svg) {
        color: var(--pine-color-accent);
      }
      .custom-loader-danger::part(loader-svg) {
        color: var(--pine-color-danger);
      }
    </style>

    <pds-button class="custom-loader-accent" variant="primary" loading="true">Accent Loader</pds-button>
    <pds-button class="custom-loader-danger" variant="secondary" loading="true">Danger Loader</pds-button>
    `
  <style>{`
    .custom-loader-accent::part(loader-svg) {
      color: var(--pine-color-accent);
    }
    .custom-loader-danger::part(loader-svg) {
      color: var(--pine-color-danger);
    }
  `}</style>

  <pds-button class="custom-loader-accent" variant="primary" loading="true">Accent Loader</pds-button>
  <pds-button class="custom-loader-danger" variant="secondary" loading="true">Danger Loader</pds-button>

### Icon Only

The icon-only prop allows a `pds-button` to display an icon only.

While the text is visually hidden, it is still remains accessible.

> ***Note:*** An icon is required to be provided.

    react: `
    <PdsButton variant="primary" iconOnly="true"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></PdsIcon>Icon Only
    </PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="secondary" iconOnly="true"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></PdsIcon>Icon Only
    </PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="accent" iconOnly="true"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></PdsIcon>Icon Only</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="destructive" iconOnly="true"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></PdsIcon>Icon Only</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="tertiary" iconOnly="true"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></PdsIcon>Icon Only
    </PdsButton>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="secondary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="accent" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="destructive" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="tertiary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
    `
  <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="secondary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="accent" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="destructive" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="tertiary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Icon Only</pds-button>

### Sizes

Buttons come in three sizes: default, small, and micro. The size prop allows you to control the button's height and spacing.

- **Default**: Standard button size - used when no size prop is specified
- **Small**: Smaller button size
- **Micro**: Smallest button size with reduced font size

    react: `
    <PdsButton variant="primary">Default</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="primary" size="small">Small</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="primary" size="micro">Micro</PdsButton>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-button variant="primary">Default</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="primary" size="small">Small</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="primary" size="micro">Micro</pds-button>
    `
  <pds-button variant="primary">Default</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="primary" size="small">Small</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="primary" size="micro">Micro</pds-button>

#### Icon Only Sizes

Sizes also apply to icon-only buttons, adjusting the button dimensions accordingly.

    react: `
    <PdsButton variant="primary" iconOnly="true"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></PdsIcon>Default</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="primary" iconOnly="true" size="small"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite" size="var(--pine-dimension-sm)"></PdsIcon>Small</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="primary" iconOnly="true" size="micro"><PdsIcon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite" size="var(--pine-dimension-150)"></PdsIcon>Micro</PdsButton>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Default</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true" size="small"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite" size="var(--pine-dimension-sm)"></pds-icon>Small</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true" size="micro"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite" size="var(--pine-dimension-150)"></pds-icon>Micro</pds-button>
    `
  <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite"></pds-icon>Default</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true" size="small"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite" size="var(--pine-dimension-sm)"></pds-icon>Small</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="primary" icon-only="true" size="micro"><pds-icon slot="start" aria-hidden="true" name="favorite" size="var(--pine-dimension-150)"></pds-icon>Micro</pds-button>

### Button Link

The button link variant allows a `pds-button` to function as a link. By providing an `href` attribute, the button will render as an anchor (`<a>`) element while maintaining the visual appearance of a button. This is useful for creating call-to-action buttons that navigate to external resources or different parts of your application.

> ***Note:*** When using the `href` attribute, button-specific props such as `type`, `name`, and `value` will be ignored. The component will maintain the same visual appearance but function as a link.

    react: `
    <PdsButton variant="primary" href="#">Create a product</PdsButton>
    <PdsButton variant="secondary" href="#">Join community</PdsButton>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-button variant="primary" href="#">Create a product</pds-button>
    <pds-button variant="secondary" href="#">Join community</pds-button>
    `
  <pds-button variant="primary" href="#">Create a product</pds-button>
  <pds-button variant="secondary" href="#">Join community</pds-button>

### Type

The type prop allows a `pds-button` to set a [button type attribute](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/button#attr-type).

> ***Note:*** The `type` prop does not apply to buttons with an `href` attribute. When an `href` is provided, the button will render as an anchor (`<a>`) element, and the types will be ignored.

#### Default (Button)

The button has no default click behavior. It can have client-side scripts listen to the element's events, which are triggered when the events occur.

#### Submit

The button submits the form data to the server.

#### Reset

The button resets all the controls to their initial values. [As noted on MDN](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/button#attr-type), this behavior tends to annoy users.

## Additional Resources

[CSS Tricks: Buttons vs. Links](https://css-tricks.com/buttons-vs-links/)

[MDN: Button Element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/button)

<Controls of={stories.Primary} />

# Checkbox

Source: https://github.com/kajabi/pine/blob/main/libs/core/src/components/pds-checkbox/docs/pds-checkbox.mdx

import * as stories from '../stories/pds-checkbox.stories.js';

import {DocArgsTable, DocCanvas} from '@pine-ds/doc-components';

<StatusBadge component="pds-checkbox" />

# Checkbox

Checkboxes provide users with selectable options like toggling a single setting or selecting multiple options from a list.

## Guidelines

### When to use
- Use checkboxes when users can select one or more options from a set.
- Ideal for situations where multiple selections can be made.

### When not to use
- Avoid using checkboxes for single-choice selections, such as in forms where only one option should be selected. In such cases, consider using radios or a switch.

### Accessibility
- Provide a clear, descriptive label for each checkbox to ensure that screen readers can identify the option effectively.
- The `aria-describedby` attribute is used to associate the checkbox with an error message or helper message but may not be read out by all screen readers.

## Properties

<DocArgsTable componentName="pds-checkbox" docSource={components} />

## Examples

### Default

    react: `<PdsCheckbox componentId="default" label="Label" />`,
    webComponent: `<pds-checkbox component-id="default" label="Label"></pds-checkbox>`
  <pds-checkbox component-id="default" label="Label"></pds-checkbox>

### Checked

Checkboxes appear as checked when activated.

    react: `<PdsCheckbox componentId="checked" label="Label" checked />`,
    webComponent: `<pds-checkbox component-id="checked" label="Label" checked></pds-checkbox>`
  <pds-checkbox component-id="checked" label="Label" checked></pds-checkbox>

### Indeterminate

Component `indeterminate` prop is for visual styling only.

Only JavaScript can set the object's `indeterminate` property. See [MDN Web Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#indeterminate_state_checkboxes)

    react: `<PdsCheckbox componentId="indeterminate" label="Label" checked indeterminate />`,
    webComponent: `<pds-checkbox component-id="indeterminate" label="Label" checked indeterminate></pds-checkbox>`
  <pds-checkbox component-id="indeterminate" label="Label" checked indeterminate></pds-checkbox>

### Disabled

Disabled visually indicates and functionally prevents interaction with the checkbox.

    react: `<PdsCheckbox componentId="disabled" label="Label" disabled />`,
    webComponent: `<pds-checkbox component-id="disabled" label="Label" disabled></pds-checkbox>`
  <pds-checkbox component-id="disabled" label="Label" disabled></pds-checkbox>

### Message

Message is a string of text that displays below the label text.

    react: `<PdsCheckbox componentId="message1" label="Label" helperMessage="This is short message text." />`,
    webComponent: `<pds-checkbox component-id="message1" label="Label" helper-message="This is short message text."></pds-checkbox>`
  <pds-checkbox component-id="message1" label="Label" helper-message="This is short message text."></pds-checkbox>

### Invalid

Displays the checkbox in an invalid state, such as when required but not checked.

An optional error message can be displayed for additional instructions, shown independently from the helper message.

    react: `<PdsCheckbox componentId="invalid" label="Label" invalid errorMessage="This is a short error message" />`,
    webComponent: `<pds-checkbox component-id="invalid" label="Label" invalid error-message="This is a short error message"></pds-checkbox>`
  <pds-checkbox component-id="invalid" label="Label" invalid error-message="This is a short error message"></pds-checkbox>

## Events

### pdsCheckboxChange
Used when you want to perform an action when the checkbox state changes. The returned structure is a `CheckboxChangeEventDetail` that contains `checked` and `value`.

## Form Integration

- Set the `name` attribute so each checked box contributes its `value` to `FormData`; unchecked boxes are omitted automatically.
- Give every checkbox in a group a distinct `value` so the server can differentiate selections.
- Pair `required`, `invalid`, and `errorMessage` when you need inline validation.

## Additional Resources

[MDN Web Docs: Checkboxes](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox)

[MDN Web Docs: Indeterminate State](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/input/checkbox#indeterminate_state_checkboxes)

## Playground

# Chip

Source: https://github.com/kajabi/pine/blob/main/libs/core/src/components/pds-chip/docs/pds-chip.mdx

import * as stories from '../stories/pds-chip.stories.js';

# Chip

Chips are used to inform users about the status of an object or to associate properties with a parent. Commonly used in tabular data to indicate status.

## Guidelines

### When to use
- To represent compact labels, statuses, or categories.
- Ideal for conveying additional metadata in components like tables, cards, or filters.
- Useful for dismissible tags or quick user actions.

### When not to use
- Avoid using Chips for long, descriptive information.
- Do not use Chips as a primary action element in a UI.

### Accessibility

The `dropdown` variant and the icon within the `tag` variant of the chip component both render as a button and will inherit all accessibility attributes of a standard HTML button.

## Properties

<DocArgsTable componentName="pds-chip" docSource={components} />

## Examples

### Default

    react: '<PdsChip>Label</PdsChip>',
    webComponent: '<pds-chip>Label</pds-chip>'
  <pds-chip>Label</pds-chip>

### Sentiment

The `sentiment` property represents the named color scheme of the chip component.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="accent">Accent</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="brand">Brand</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger">Danger</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info">Info</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="neutral">Neutral</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="success">Success</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning">Warning</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="accent">Accent</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="brand">Brand</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger">Danger</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info">Info</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="neutral">Neutral</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="success">Success</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning">Warning</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="accent">Accent</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="brand">Brand</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger">Danger</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info">Info</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="neutral">Neutral</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="success">Success</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning">Warning</pds-chip>

#### Brand

> **IMPORTANT**: The `brand` sentiment is a special case where only `icon` and `size` properties are supported.
> The `dot`, `dropdown`, and `tag` properties are not supported by design.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="brand">Brand</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="brand" icon="product">Brand</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="brand" size="lg">Brand</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="brand">Brand</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="brand" icon="product">Brand</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="brand" size="lg">Brand</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="brand">Brand</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="brand" icon="product">Brand</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="brand" size="lg">Brand</pds-chip>

### Dot

A small circular indicator displayed within a chip. Dot colors are determined by the `sentiment` prop.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="accent" dot>Accent</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger" dot>Danger</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" dot>Info</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="neutral" dot>Neutral</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="success" dot>Success</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning" dot>Warning</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="accent" dot>Accent</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger" dot>Danger</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" dot>Info</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" dot>Neutral</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="success" dot>Success</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning" dot>Warning</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="accent" dot>Accent</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger" dot>Danger</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" dot>Info</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" dot>Neutral</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="success" dot>Success</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning" dot>Warning</pds-chip>

### Icon

The `icon` property can be used to display an icon within a chip.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="accent" icon="archive">Accent</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="brand" icon="product">Brand</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger" icon="danger">Danger</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" icon="info-circle">Info</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="neutral" icon="tag">Neutral</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="success" icon="check">Success</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning" icon="check">Warning</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="accent" icon="archive">Accent</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="brand" icon="product">Brand</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger" icon="danger">Danger</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" icon="info-circle">Info</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" icon="tag">Neutral</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="success" icon="check">Success</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning" icon="warning">Warning</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="accent" icon="archive">Accent</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="brand" icon="product">Brand</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger" icon="danger">Danger</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" icon="info-circle">Info</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" icon="tag">Neutral</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="success" icon="check">Success</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning" icon="warning">Warning</pds-chip>

### Dropdown

If the `variant` property is set to `"dropdown"`, the chip will be rendered in a dropdown style, altering its appearance and behavior accordingly.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="accent" variant="dropdown">Accent</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger" variant="dropdown">Danger</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" variant="dropdown">Info</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="neutral" variant="dropdown">Neutral</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="success" variant="dropdown">Success</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning" variant="dropdown">Warning</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="accent" variant="dropdown">Accent</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger" variant="dropdown">Danger</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="dropdown">Info</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" variant="dropdown">Neutral</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="success" variant="dropdown">Success</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning" variant="dropdown">Warning</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="accent" variant="dropdown">Accent</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger" variant="dropdown">Danger</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="dropdown">Info</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" variant="dropdown">Neutral</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="success" variant="dropdown">Success</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning" variant="dropdown">Warning</pds-chip>

### Tag

If the `variant` property is set to `"tag"`, the chip will be rendered in a tag style, altering its appearance and behavior accordingly.

Tag is often used to represent a selected item or a removable element and includes a close button that can be clicked to perform an associated action.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger" variant="tag">Danger</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" variant="tag">Info</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="neutral" variant="tag">Neutral</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="success" variant="tag">Success</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning" variant="tag">Warning</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger" variant="tag">Danger</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="tag">Info</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" variant="tag">Neutral</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="success" variant="tag">Success</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning" variant="tag">Warning</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger" variant="tag">Danger</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="tag">Info</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" variant="tag">Neutral</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="success" variant="tag">Success</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning" variant="tag">Warning</pds-chip>

#### Tag with Remove URL

The `remove-url` property allows the tag's close button to function as a link, enabling URL-based removal actions. This is particularly useful in data tables and filters where you want to remove items by navigating to a URL instead of handling removal with JavaScript.

When `remove-url` is provided, the close button is rendered as an `<a>` element instead of a `<button>`, and the `pdsTagCloseClick` event is still emitted for backward compatibility.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="neutral" variant="tag" removeUrl="/filters/remove/1">Filter 1</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" variant="tag" removeUrl="/tags/active">Active</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" variant="tag" remove-url="/filters/remove/1">Filter 1</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="tag" remove-url="/tags/active">Active</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="neutral" variant="tag" remove-url="/filters/remove/1">Filter 1</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="tag" remove-url="/tags/active">Active</pds-chip>

#### Tag with HTTP Method

The `remove-http-method` property adds `data-method` and `data-turbo-method` attributes to the remove link, enabling Rails/Turbo framework compatibility for non-GET HTTP requests. This is useful for DELETE operations or other HTTP methods.

> **Note**: The `remove-http-method` property only applies when `remove-url` is provided.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger" variant="tag" removeUrl="/tags/1" removeHttpMethod="delete">Delete Me</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning" variant="tag" removeUrl="/tags/2" removeHttpMethod="post">Post Action</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger" variant="tag" remove-url="/tags/1" remove-http-method="delete">Delete Me</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning" variant="tag" remove-url="/tags/2" remove-http-method="post">Post Action</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger" variant="tag" remove-url="/tags/1" remove-http-method="delete">Delete Me</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning" variant="tag" remove-url="/tags/2" remove-http-method="post">Post Action</pds-chip>

#### Tag with Remove Target

The `remove-target` property specifies where to open the linked document when the remove button is clicked. This is useful when you want the removal action to open in a new tab or specific browsing context.

> **Note**: The `remove-target` property only applies when `remove-url` is provided.

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" variant="tag" removeUrl="/clear-filters" removeTarget="_blank">Clear (New Tab)</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="tag" remove-url="/clear-filters" remove-target="_blank">Clear (New Tab)</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" variant="tag" remove-url="/clear-filters" remove-target="_blank">Clear (New Tab)</pds-chip>

### Sizes

The `size` property controls the visual size of the chip. Available sizes are `sm` (small), `md` (medium/default), and `lg` (large).

    react: `
    <PdsChip size="sm">Small</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip>Medium</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip size="lg">Large</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip size="sm">Small</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip>Medium</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip size="lg">Large</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip size="sm">Small</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip>Medium</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip size="lg">Large</pds-chip>

Sizes work across all variants and sentiments:

    react: `
    <PdsChip sentiment="success" size="sm" dot>Small</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger" size="sm" variant="tag">Small</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" size="sm" variant="dropdown">Small</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning" size="sm" icon="warning">Small</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="success" size="lg" dot>Large</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="danger" size="lg" variant="tag">Large</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="info" size="lg" variant="dropdown">Large</PdsChip>
    <PdsChip sentiment="warning" size="lg" icon="warning">Large</PdsChip>
    `,
    webComponent: `
    <pds-chip sentiment="success" size="sm" dot>Small</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger" size="sm" variant="tag">Small</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" size="sm" variant="dropdown">Small</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning" size="sm" icon="warning">Small</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="success" size="lg" dot>Large</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="danger" size="lg" variant="tag">Large</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="info" size="lg" variant="dropdown">Large</pds-chip>
    <pds-chip sentiment="warning" size="lg" icon="warning">Large</pds-chip>
    `
  <pds-chip sentiment="success" size="sm" dot>Small</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger" size="sm" variant="tag">Small</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" size="sm" variant="dropdown">Small</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning" size="sm" icon="warning">Small</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="success" size="lg" dot>Large</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="danger" size="lg" variant="tag">Large</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="info" size="lg" variant="dropdown">Large</pds-chip>
  <pds-chip sentiment="warning" size="lg" icon="warning">Large</pds-chip>

# Combobox

Source: https://github.com/kajabi/pine/blob/main/libs/core/src/components/pds-combobox/docs/pds-combobox.mdx

import * as stories from '../stories/pds-combobox.stories.js';

import { DocArgsTable, DocCanvas } from '@pine-ds/doc-components';

<StatusBadge component="pds-combobox" />

# Combobox

A combobox is a text input with a dropdown list of options, allowing users to filter and select from a list. It is useful for searchable selects and autocomplete scenarios.

## Guidelines

### When to use
- When users need to select from a long or searchable list of options.
- When you want to allow both typing and selection.
- When you need rich layouts in options or trigger content.

### When not to use
- For simple, short lists (use [Select](/docs/components-select--docs)).
- For multi-select (use checkboxes or a multi-select component).

### Accessibility
- Implements the WAI-ARIA Combobox Pattern for screen reader compatibility.
- Supports full keyboard navigation: Arrow keys, Enter, Escape.
- Input is labelled and controls the listbox.
- Custom layouts maintain proper ARIA attributes and focus management.

## Usage Notes

### Working with Labels

When analyzing designs or screenshots, text that appears above an input field is the input's label, not a separate `pds-text` component. The `label` prop creates text that appears above the input field and integrates properly with the component's styling and accessibility features.

## Properties

<DocArgsTable componentName="pds-combobox" docSource={components} />

## Modes

The combobox supports two modes:

- **Filtering** (`mode="filter"`): Filters options as you type (default).
- **Select-only** (`mode="select-only"`): Always shows all options, regardless of input value.

Use the `mode` prop to control this behavior.

## Triggers

The combobox supports three trigger types:

- **Input** (`trigger="input"`): Renders a text input (default, for filtering/autocomplete).
- **Button** (`trigger="button"`): Renders a button-like div (for select-only, non-editable comboboxes).
- **Chip** (`trigger="chip"`): Renders a chip component (for select-only, styled as a chip).

Use the `trigger` prop to control this behavior. See [WAI-ARIA Combobox Patterns](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/#examples) for more details.

## Trigger Variants

The button trigger supports the following visual variants, matching Pine button styles:

- **secondary** (default)
- **primary**
- **accent**
- **destructive**

Use the `triggerVariant` prop to control the style.

### Secondary (default)
The secondary variant provides a subtle button appearance with a white background and border. This is the default styling for button triggers.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-secondary" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-trigger-secondary" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" triggerVariant="secondary" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-secondary" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Primary
The primary variant uses Pine's primary color scheme, creating a more prominent button appearance suitable for primary actions.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-primary" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="primary" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-trigger-primary" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" triggerVariant="primary" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-primary" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="primary" mode="select-only">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Accent
The accent variant uses Pine's accent color scheme, providing a distinctive appearance for special or highlighted selections.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-accent" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="accent" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-trigger-accent" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" triggerVariant="accent" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-accent" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="accent" mode="select-only">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Destructive
The destructive variant uses Pine's destructive color scheme, providing a warning appearance suitable for destructive or dangerous actions like deleting items.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-destructive" label="Delete Item" placeholder="Select item to delete" trigger="button" trigger-variant="destructive" mode="select-only">
  <option value="file1">Document.pdf</option>
  <option value="file2">Image.jpg</option>
  <option value="file3">Spreadsheet.xlsx</option>
  <option value="file4">Presentation.pptx</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-trigger-destructive" label="Delete Item" placeholder="Select item to delete" trigger="button" triggerVariant="destructive" mode="select-only">
  <option value="file1">Document.pdf</option>
  <option value="file2">Image.jpg</option>
  <option value="file3">Spreadsheet.xlsx</option>
  <option value="file4">Presentation.pptx</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-destructive" label="Delete Item" placeholder="Select item to delete" trigger="button" trigger-variant="destructive" mode="select-only">
    <option value="file1">Document.pdf</option>
    <option value="file2">Image.jpg</option>
    <option value="file3">Spreadsheet.xlsx</option>
    <option value="file4">Presentation.pptx</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Filtering (default)
In filtering mode, the combobox filters the available options as you type, making it easy to find specific items in large lists. This is the default behavior.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-filter" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search...">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-filter" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search...">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-filter" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search...">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Select-only
In select-only mode, all options are always shown regardless of what you type. This is useful when you want dropdown behavior without filtering.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-selectonly" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search..." mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-selectonly" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search..." mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-selectonly" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search..." mode="select-only">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Input Trigger (default)
The input trigger provides a text input field that users can type into. This is ideal for filtering and autocomplete scenarios where users need to search through options.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-input" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search..." trigger="input">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-trigger-input" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search..." trigger="input">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-input" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Type to search..." trigger="input">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Button Trigger (select-only)
The button trigger renders as a button-like element instead of a text input. This is perfect for select-only scenarios where users choose from a dropdown without typing.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-button" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-trigger-button" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" mode="select-only">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-button" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" mode="select-only">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Chip Trigger (select-only)
The chip trigger renders as a chip component instead of a text input or button. This provides a more compact, tag-like appearance perfect for select-only scenarios where you want the trigger to look like a chip.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="chip-draft" label="Status" trigger="chip" mode="select-only" value="draft">
  <option value="draft" chip-sentiment="neutral" chip-dot="true">Draft</option>
  <option value="published" chip-sentiment="success" chip-dot="true">Published</option>
  <option value="archived" chip-sentiment="warning" chip-dot="true">Archived</option>
</pds-combobox>`,

  <option value="published" chip-sentiment="success" chip-dot="true">Published</option>
  <option value="archived" chip-sentiment="warning" chip-dot="true">Archived</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="chip-draft" label="Status" trigger="chip" mode="select-only" value="draft">
    <option value="draft" chip-sentiment="neutral" chip-dot="true">Draft</option>
    <option value="published" chip-sentiment="success" chip-dot="true">Published</option>
    <option value="archived" chip-sentiment="warning" chip-dot="true">Archived</option>

## Preselected Options

The combobox supports preselecting options using the `value` property on the combobox component. This approach is consistent with other form components and works well with frameworks like React.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-preselected-value" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" mode="select-only" value="panda">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-preselected-value" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" mode="select-only" value="panda">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-preselected-value" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" mode="select-only" value="panda">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Preselection with Input Trigger

Preselection also works with input triggers, showing the selected option's text in the input field:

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-preselected-input" label="Favorite Color" placeholder="Type to search..." mode="filter" trigger="input" value="blue">
  <option value="red">Red</option>
  <option value="blue">Blue</option>
  <option value="green">Green</option>
  <option value="yellow">Yellow</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-preselected-input" label="Favorite Color" placeholder="Type to search..." mode="filter" trigger="input" value="blue">
  <option value="red">Red</option>
  <option value="blue">Blue</option>
  <option value="green">Green</option>
  <option value="yellow">Yellow</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-preselected-input" label="Favorite Color" placeholder="Type to search..." mode="filter" trigger="input" value="blue">
    <option value="red">Red</option>
    <option value="blue">Blue</option>
    <option value="green">Green</option>
    <option value="yellow">Yellow</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Important Notes

- **Value vs. Display Text**: When using the `value` property, provide the option's `value` attribute (e.g., `value="panda"`), not the display text. The combobox will automatically show the corresponding option's text content (e.g., "Panda").
- **Form Integration**: Preselected options work seamlessly with forms and will be included in form submissions.
- **Dynamic Updates**: The `value` property can be updated programmatically to change the selection at runtime.

## Sizing and Positioning

You can control the dropdown's placement, width, and height, as well as the trigger width using the following props:

- `dropdownPlacement`: 'bottom-start' | 'bottom-end' | 'top-start' | 'top-end' (default: 'bottom-start')
- `dropdownMount`: 'host' | 'body' (default: 'host') — also known as an “append to body” pattern; use `body` inside scrollable modals or other `overflow: hidden` containers so the list is not clipped. When `body` is used, the portal mounts inside the nearest `<dialog>` when present (including `pds-modal` / `showModal()`), resolving through slots and shadow roots so the list stays in the top layer; otherwise on `document.body`. Keyboard focus stays on the trigger (via `aria-activedescendant`) so modal focus traps keep working.
- Listbox `id` and `aria-controls` use `${componentId}-listbox` (for example `my-combobox-listbox`), not a shared `pds-combobox-listbox` id. Option row `id` values use `${componentId}-option-${index}` for unique `aria-activedescendant` when multiple comboboxes exist on the page.
- `dropdownWidth`: Any valid CSS width value (default: '236px')
- `triggerWidth`: Any valid CSS width value for both input and button triggers (default: 'fit-content')
- `max-height`: Any valid CSS height value (e.g., '200px', '10rem') to limit dropdown height with scrolling

### Custom Placement
You can control where the dropdown appears relative to the trigger element. This example shows the dropdown aligned to the right edge (`bottom-end`).

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-placement-end" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" dropdown-placement="bottom-end">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-placement-end" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" dropdown-placement="bottom-end">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-placement-end" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" dropdown-placement="bottom-end">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>
  </pds-combobox>

### Custom Dropdown Width
The dropdown width can be customized using any valid CSS width value. This example sets the dropdown to 300px wide.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-width-custom" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" dropdown-width="300px">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</pds-combobox>`,
    react: `<PdsCombobox componentId="combobox-width-custom" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" dropdown-width="300px">
  <option value="cat">Cat</option>
  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-width-custom" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" dropdown-width="300px">
    <option value="cat">Cat</option>
    <option value="dog">Dog</option>
    <option value="panda">Panda</option>
    <option value="snake">Snake</option>

### Custom Trigger Width
The trigger width can be customized for both input and button triggers using any valid CSS width value. This example sets the button trigger to 300px wide.

    webComponent: `<pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-width-custom" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" trigger-width="300px">

  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>

  <option value="dog">Dog</option>
  <option value="panda">Panda</option>
  <option value="snake">Snake</option>
</PdsCombobox>`,
  }}
>
  <pds-combobox component-id="combobox-trigger-width-custom" label="Favorite Animal" placeholder="Select an animal" trigger="button" trigger-variant="secondary" mode="select-only" trigger-width="300px">
